subject: David Todisco City Council Candidate Interview
overview: Host Danielle Balocca interviewed City Council candidate David Todisco regarding his campaign platform and vision for Medford. Todisco discussed infrastructure priorities, charter reform, and the strategic allocation of federal pandemic relief funds.

items.title: Candidate Introduction
items.summary: Danielle Balocca introduced David Todisco, outlining his background as a student leader in Medford and his professional experience in congressional press offices.

items.title: Local Background and Inspiration
items.summary: Todisco discussed his favorite Medford businesses and credited a high school history teacher for inspiring his commitment to civic engagement.

items.title: Professional Path to Politics
items.summary: The candidate described his political trajectory, including founding the College Democrats at UMass Lowell and working for various federal campaigns.

items.title: Motivations for City Council Run
items.summary: Todisco stated that he decided to run after observing divided discourse during televised council meetings and a lack of responsiveness to resident concerns regarding equity.

items.title: Federal Relief Fund Allocation
items.summary: Todisco advocated for using federal American Rescue Plan funds to install proper ventilation at Medford High School and repair ADA-compliant city infrastructure.

items.title: Charter Reform and Representation
items.summary: The discussion covered the need for a charter review to implement ward-based representation, four-year mayoral terms, and citywide multilingual communications.

items.title: Housing Insecurity and Zoning
items.summary: To address the local housing crisis, Todisco proposed creating an Office of Affordable Housing and rezoning Mystic Avenue to increase housing stock.

items.title: Medford Square Revitalization
items.summary: The candidate argued that the city should stop conducting studies and begin implementing existing plans to modernize and revitalize Medford Square.

items.title: Environmental Equity and Forestry
items.summary: Todisco prioritized expanding the city's tree canopy, specifically highlighting the lack of greenery in South Medford as an issue of neighborhood equity.

items.title: Municipal Finance and Taxation
items.summary: Regarding city revenue, Todisco suggested that tax override questions should go to the ballot while maintaining protections for seniors on fixed incomes.

items.title: Election Participation and Voting
items.summary: The interview concluded with a call for residents to participate in the election via early voting, mail-in ballots, or poll voting on Election Day.
